whatItDoes: Encodes latitude/longitude to geohash (precision 1–12) and decodes geohash to center, bounds, error, and 8 neighbors. Shows bounds as min/max lat/lng and a map placeholder. Pure JS, no map dep.
whyItExists: Geohashes are used for spatial indexing and proximity search. Manual base32 math is tedious; this does it locally with neighbor calc for bounding-box queries without calling a maps API.
whoShouldUse: Backend developers indexing locations, mobile devs debugging nearby queries, and GIS learners exploring geohash precision.
useCases: Encode 37.7749,-122.4194 precision 9 → 9q8yyk8yt for a DB key
Decode 9q8yyk8yt → center/bounds/neighbors for a bounding-box query
Compare precision 5 vs 9 to see error radius
instructions: In Encode, enter lat/lng and pick precision 1–12, click Encode to get geohash and bounds.
In Decode, paste a geohash, click Decode to see center, bounds, and 8 neighbors in a grid.
Copy any value from the output (data-testid). All math is local — no upload.
bestPractices: Use precision 5 for city, 9 for building; higher precision = smaller error but longer hash
Use neighbors to expand a bounding-box search beyond the base cell
commonMistakes: Entering lng outside −180..180 — the encoder clamps but shows an error
Expecting decode to return the original lat/lng exactly — it returns the cell center, not the input point
faq: Is it uploaded? No — base32 encode/decode is pure JS in your browser.
Does it need a map? No — a placeholder div is shown; integrate Leaflet if you need a visual map.
What base32 alphabet? 0123456789bcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz (no a,i,l,o) per geohash spec.
